title: percept2vec: animals
blurb: 120 photos of animals, as people rated them (every pair, 0–10, ten raters each) and as DINOv2 sees them.

notes.rsa: People sort strictly by kind: 96% of each photo’s five nearest neighbours are in its group, against 85% for DINOv2. Closing that gap is what Peterson et al. set out to do.

metricNote: Here: people’s distance is 10 − the mean similarity rating (0–10, ten raters per pair); DINOv2’s is cosine.

about.name: percept2vec
about.quote: Datasets and API (coming soon) for fitting CNN representations to human similarity judgments for images
about.label: GitHub (Joshua Peterson)

about.name: Adapting Deep Network Features to Capture Psychological Representations
about.quote: There were 7,140 possible image comparisons, each of which was rated by 10 unique participants, for a total of 71,400 ratings from 209 different participants.
about.label: CogSci 2016 (arXiv)

here: Here: all 120 animal photographs, as 10 − the mean of people’s 0–10 similarity ratings (A) and as DINOv2 embeddings under cosine distance (B). The release numbers the photos; the names are ours. Groups are the nine clusters the authors found in the ratings.
